stem: What is Prompt Builder?

options.text: A Setup tool for creating and managing prompt templates
A reporting tool that tracks AI usage by team
A Data Loader feature that imports prompt files
A kind of profile that controls access to prompts

explanation: Prompt Builder lets admins write, ground, test and activate prompt templates.

stem: Which template type fills a field with generated text, such as a summary?

options.text: Field generation
Sales email
Flex
Record summary only for chat

explanation: Field generation templates write text into a field on a record.

stem: Which template type drafts an email to a contact or lead?

options.text: Sales email
Field generation
Record summary
Flex

explanation: Sales email templates generate email drafts from record data.

stem: Which template type is general-purpose with inputs you define?

options.text: Flex
Sales email
Field generation
Record summary

explanation: Flex templates take custom inputs and are the most general type.

stem: What does a merge field do in a prompt template?

options.text: Inserts data from a record into the prompt
Merges two templates into a single longer prompt
Merges two accounts that share the same name
Deletes the prompt after it has been run once

explanation: Merge fields ground the prompt with real data from the record and related records.

stem: What is grounding?

options.text: Adding real company data to the prompt so the answer is based on facts
Training a new language model on your company's records
Hiding sensitive values before the prompt reaches the model
Auditing each model response after it is generated

explanation: Grounding supplies data in the prompt. It does not retrain the model.

stem: An AI summary is wrong because the account's address is out of date. What should the admin do?

options.text: Fix the data
Retrain the language model
Turn on masking
Rewrite the Trust Layer

explanation: If the data is wrong, fix the data. Grounding passes along whatever is in the record.

stem: Where can an admin check what data was inserted into a prompt before it goes to the model?

options.text: The resolved prompt in the preview
The Setup Audit Trail, which logs changes to settings
The report folder where the template is stored
The login history of the user who runs the template

explanation: Previewing a template shows the resolved prompt with merge fields filled in.

stem: What must an admin do for users to use a new prompt template in the app?

options.text: Activate a version of the template
Delete the old template so the new one is used
Convert it into a report that users can run
Recreate it as a flow and add it to the page

explanation: Templates must be activated before they can be used.

stem: When a user runs a prompt template, whose data access applies to the merge fields?

options.text: The running user's access
Always the admin's access
No access checks apply
The CEO's access

explanation: The Trust Layer's secure retrieval respects the user's permissions.

stem: What is the Einstein Trust Layer?

options.text: Security and privacy controls around calls to language models
A kind of profile that gives users access to AI features
A report type that shows AI usage by user
A backup service that copies prompts to another region

explanation: It protects data used with generative AI through retrieval controls, masking, zero data retention, toxicity detection and audit.

stem: Which Trust Layer feature replaces sensitive values with placeholders before they leave Salesforce?

options.text: Data masking
Toxicity detection
Audit trail
Prompt activation

explanation: Data masking hides sensitive values from the model and unmasks them in the response.

stem: What does zero data retention mean?

options.text: The model provider does not store your prompts and responses or use them for training
Salesforce deletes all of your data once a month
No data is ever sent to a model, so nothing can be stored
The audit trail is empty because nothing is logged by Salesforce

explanation: Zero data retention is an agreement with the model provider that data is not kept or used to train models.

stem: Which Trust Layer feature scans responses for harmful content?

options.text: Toxicity detection
Data masking
Grounding
Prompt activation

explanation: Toxicity detection checks responses for harmful or inappropriate content.

stem: Which Trust Layer feature records the prompt, response and feedback for review?

options.text: Audit trail
Masking
Grounding
Zero retention

explanation: The audit trail stores what was sent and returned so you can review it.

stem: A legal team asks if the Trust Layer must be bought separately before go-live. What is the best answer?

options.text: It is built into Agentforce on the Salesforce Platform
It is a separate subscription for each agent
It is a third-party product
It only applies to Slack

explanation: The Trust Layer is part of the Agentforce platform architecture rather than a separate add-on.

stem: How can an admin limit who may build or run prompt templates?

options.text: Through permission sets for prompt template access
Through page layouts assigned to each profile
Through report folders shared with each team
Through the fiscal year settings of the org

explanation: Access is granted with permissions such as the Prompt Template Manager permission set.

objective: Explain why data quality decides AI results
stem: Which of these most directly affects the quality of AI summaries of accounts?

options.text: Clean, de-duplicated and complete data
The logo shown on the org's login page and mobile app
The number of dashboards that the sales team has built
The fiscal year setting that reports use for each quarter

explanation: AI relies on the quality of the data it can see, so duplicates and gaps lead to wrong outputs.

objective: Explain why data quality decides AI results
stem: Why does the exam give Data and Analytics Management the largest weight, in connection with AI?

options.text: Because clean, governed data is the foundation for AI and automation
Because reports are AI and need the most study time
Because dashboards train the AI model on their own
Because AI replaces data and so makes it less important

explanation: Salesforce emphasises that high-quality data underpins automation and AI results.

stem: Which practice keeps AI responsible for customer-affecting decisions?

options.text: Keep a human in the loop and test for bias
Let the AI decide alone, so that results are consistent
Skip testing to launch faster and fix issues later
Turn off the audit trail to protect customer privacy

explanation: Human review, transparency and testing help prevent harm.

stem: Before launching a new AI feature, what is a sensible first step?

options.text: Test with real past examples and have the business mark them
Launch to all customers, then fix problems as they appear
Delete old data so the AI starts with a clean slate
Turn off permissions so the AI cannot make mistakes

explanation: A dry run with realistic cases catches problems before customers see them.

stem: Which South African law affects how personal information may be used with AI?

options.text: POPIA
GDPR only
No law applies
The fiscal year rules

explanation: POPIA regulates processing of personal information in South Africa, so check purpose and consent.

stem: Which statement about prompts is true?

options.text: Specific prompts with examples and clear refusals give better results
Short vague prompts give the best results for every task
Prompts never need testing once they are saved
Prompts cannot use record data, only typed text

explanation: Clear instructions, examples and boundaries improve outputs.

stem: A customer asks what protects their personal data when a prompt is sent to a language model. Which best describes the Trust Layer?

options.text: Masking, zero data retention, toxicity detection and an audit trail around model calls
A separate profile that blocks every AI user from reaching any object in the org
A sharing rule that limits the models to Public Read Only access on the data
A larger storage limit for the prompts that are stored in the org each month

explanation: The Trust Layer adds data masking, secure retrieval, zero data retention, toxicity detection and audit around calls to language models.
